objective: Add optional OpenTofu S3/GCS archive source locations to Cloud IaC module-registry download responses while preserving local-foundation-only scope and no live object-store runtime claim.

best_practice_sources.what_it_establishes: OpenTofu module sources can use private registries, archive URLs, S3 archive sources with s3::https://, and GCS archive sources with gcs::https://.
The module-registry download endpoint returns a location value from which OpenTofu downloads the module source.
S3 object integrity is tied to checksum validation; this ChangeSet does not implement live S3 upload/download checksum enforcement.
Cloud Storage objects carry metadata such as generation and checksums; generation/version enforcement remains future work.
Cloud Storage supports request preconditions for safe object operations; no live object-store write/read precondition is claimed here.

red_tests.summary: The app object-source nonclaim constant and loader behavior were absent. After adding app parsing, the domain source validator still rejected s3::https:// archive sources as MissingSourceVersionPin.

implemented_claims: Cloud IaC domain release source validation now accepts OpenTofu S3 and GCS archive source locations when the archive filename remains pinned to the module version.
The app release-index loader accepts optional archive_source_location and validates it as s3::https:// or gcs::https:// without credentials, query strings, fragments, whitespace, or filename drift.
When archive_source_location is present, module-registry download JSON returns that source location instead of /artifacts/modules/<archive>.zip.
Object-source-backed modules are not registered in the local artifact route map, avoiding a local artifact-serving fallback for that module.
Manifest, catalog, tasks, and evidence record the opentofu-s3-gcs-source-location-no-live-object-store-no-upload nonclaim.
explicit_non_claims: no IAM policy enforcement or object-store credential integration
no signed URLs, CDN, TLS termination, or deployed Cloud IaC endpoint
no registry publish API, database adapter, or persistent registry store
no production authentication runtime or Cedar policy evaluation runtime
no tenant identity, RBAC, ABAC, or IAM integration
no signed module releases, Sigstore/cosign execution, SLSA, or VSA attestation verification
no provider runtime, provider API calls, provider credentials, or cloud provisioning
no live Argo CD rollout, Kubernetes rollout, or Jenkins pipeline execution
no measured SLO, DR, sharding execution, tenant migration, or capacity telemetry
no FD-001 microservice dogfood tenant workload hosting or production tenant evidence
no aggregate ./bin/oya gate run-all success claim for current worktree
false_green_findings_closed: The app can now distinguish local artifact-route downloads from OpenTofu object-source download locations instead of treating all archive metadata as local filesystem serving.
The domain no longer rejects OpenTofu-supported S3/GCS archive source addresses solely because they lack a git-style ref query.
Object-source tests reject plain HTTPS, credential-like query strings, and mismatched archive filenames so object-source metadata cannot silently smuggle secrets or point at an unpinned archive name.
known_gaps: This is source-location support only; it does not upload to or download from S3/GCS, provision buckets, enforce object-store IAM, or verify object version/generation preconditions.
Current repo-local release-index entries still use local archive routes; no production object-store release index has been materialized.
Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required and aggregate gate run-all are not claimed by this slice.

findings: Kept the object-store step honest: add source-location contract support without pretending live object-store runtime exists.
Moves module distribution from local-only artifact routes toward cloud object archive sources that OpenTofu can consume.
Negative tests reject plain HTTPS, credential-like source markers, and mismatched object archive filenames.
The release index uses one optional archive_source_location field; existing local release indexes remain compatible.
Focused tests, full app/domain tests, and scoped HTTP/Cloud IaC matrix all passed.

alternatives_named: Implement live object-store adapters and provider credentials now
Add OpenTofu S3/GCS source-location support first
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Source-location support is the smallest honest step toward object-store-backed module distribution without inventing fake live bucket evidence.
rejected_reasons: Local-only routes block any future object-source release-index contract.
Live adapters require bucket provisioning, IAM, credentials, integrity, and generation/version evidence outside this slice.

findings: Object source locations reject credential-like markers, userinfo, queries, fragments, whitespace, and filename drift.
Object-source download response is a string selection path only; no live object-store I/O or throughput claim is made.
Object-store version/generation and retention controls remain explicit future work, not compliance evidence in this slice.
Existing release-index fixtures without archive_source_location continue to return /artifacts/modules/<archive>.zip locations.
The app fails closed at load time for malformed object source metadata instead of returning a dangerous download location later.
ChangeSet is tied to Oya VCS claim, app/domain source/tests, manifest/catalog/tasks, multispectrum evidence, and audit-chain rows.
Used Oya VCS claim; avoided raw git/gh; read root hub and operating contract; kept /plan complementary-only; did not claim production/hyperscaler completion.
No new dependencies were added. Object-source validation uses std-only string checks in the domain/app layers.

review_findings: No critical/high issues found for the local foundation scope. Live object-store integrity/versioning remains an explicit gap.
